observation.visible_scene: A conifer forest clearing with dry pale grass, a large pine trunk left-of-center, a fallen mossy log in the foreground-left, and a small tripod standing in the mid-ground left of center. From the start a low, thin white smoke/vapor plume rises from the ground in the center-right of the frame. Lighting is flat and overcast.
visible_changes: Frames 0.000–1.067 s: the scene is essentially static; only the small white ground plume slowly drifts and reshapes, extending faintly to the right. The tripod, log and trees hold fixed positions, indicating a still camera.
At 1.134 s the image becomes a uniform pale gray/white frame — a discontinuity (editing cut or full-frame overexposure flash), not continuous motion.
At 1.201 s a bright white fireball/flash erupts at the center where the tripod stands, tinting the left trees pink-orange.
1.268–1.468 s: the frame shows heavy directional motion blur (camera shake or rapid movement) while the white cloud grows.

1.535–2.669 s: the blur subsides and a large white smoke cloud billows upward and outward from the center, steadily expanding into a tall column that dominates the middle of the frame; the tripod remains visible at its base, and the surrounding trees stay in place.

The expansion is growth of the cloud volume, not translation of a solid object; the background does not shift consistently, so the apparent motion is cloud expansion plus brief camera shake rather than scene movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the initial low plume and what triggered the flash/explosion is not shown.
The state of the device/tripod before t=0 and the final dissipation of the cloud after t=2.669 s are outside the excerpt.
Whether the pale frame at 1.134 s is an edit or an overexposed flash is not determinable from these samples alone.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the white frame (cut vs. flash) is uncertain.
Camera motion during 1.268–1.468 s (shake vs. pan) cannot be separated from cloud motion with certainty.
Whether the early ground plume and the later large cloud originate from the same source is inferred, not directly visible.
